subject: physical-education
title: Correction and reflection: coaching a tactical idea to someone else under transfer
focus: coaching a tactical idea to someone else
essentialQuestion: How do experienced players decide faster than they can think?
materials: Optional: three small household objects may represent boundaries, teammates, or targets. Sport equipment, a court, and additional players are not required.
Use only soft, unbreakable household items that a trusted adult approves; imaginary equipment and paper planning are always valid substitutes.
movementCues: Start balanced with eyes scanning the whole space, not fixed on one object or person.
Move or point into open space, then recover to a position that protects the next likely option.
Decide early, communicate the choice clearly, and use controlled movement with no contact required.
Pause after the pattern and explain what cue changed the decision; good positioning matters more than speed.
Self-manage the task by rehearsing at low intensity, changing one variable at a time, and choosing control and repeatable technique over a maximal result.
ageAppropriateTechnique: Self-manage the task by rehearsing at low intensity, changing one variable at a time, and choosing control and repeatable technique over a maximal result.
spaceSetup: Clear a dry, non-slip area at least two arm-spans wide when available. Mark the boundary with visible household objects or imaginary lines, remove furniture, cords, pets, and breakables, and keep a stable chair or wall nearby if support helps. Low-space path: clear one arm-span while seated or standing and keep every movement in place.

optional: Optional: three small household objects may represent boundaries, teammates, or targets. Sport equipment, a court, and additional players are not required.
householdSubstitutes: Use only soft, unbreakable household items that a trusted adult approves; imaginary equipment and paper planning are always valid substitutes.
equipmentRequirements.equalCreditNoEquipment: Equal-credit home option: use hand signals, floor points, or a paper diagram to show ready position, open space, one decision, and recovery; then walk, wheel, gesture, or describe the pattern in a cleared area. Full transfer credit requires the designed constraint, the tactical decision it is meant to produce, the coaching cue, and a success check. Live coaching or a full solo simulation earns equal credit when it preserves all four pieces of evidence.

safetyRules: Check the floor, ceiling, footwear or mobility supports, boundary, and any optional item before moving. Keep people, pets, furniture, cords, and breakables outside the boundary.
Use a self-selected easy-to-moderate challenge, breathe continuously, and choose control over speed, force, distance, or repetition.
Rest, reduce range or pace, use support, or choose the non-movement planning path at any time without losing credit.
Use solo, shadow, or walk-through practice at home. No collision, guarding contact, wrestling, tackling, or movement toward another person is required.
stoppingRules: Stop immediately for pain, dizziness, unusual breathing difficulty, a head impact, or any movement that feels unsafe; tell a trusted adult.
Stop when a person, pet, object, or slippery surface enters the movement area. Reset the area before continuing.
After a head impact, injury, or symptoms that do not settle with rest, do not resume the activity until a trusted adult or qualified professional says it is safe.
accessibleAdaptation: Use the same cues while seated, supported by a stable chair or wall, using a mobility aid, working through a comfortable reduced range, or describing/gesturing the movement when movement is not appropriate. Work solo or with one trusted adult. The adapted path is assessed for the same control, decision, and explanation and earns equal credit. Full transfer credit requires the designed constraint, the tactical decision it is meant to produce, the coaching cue, and a success check. Live coaching or a full solo simulation earns equal credit when it preserves all four pieces of evidence.
lowSpaceNoEquipmentAlternative: Equal-credit home option: use hand signals, floor points, or a paper diagram to show ready position, open space, one decision, and recovery; then walk, wheel, gesture, or describe the pattern in a cleared area. Full transfer credit requires the designed constraint, the tactical decision it is meant to produce, the coaching cue, and a success check. Live coaching or a full solo simulation earns equal credit when it preserves all four pieces of evidence.
activitySteps: Setup: read the equipment, space, safety, stop, and transfer-evidence rules; clear the area and choose the standard or adapted path.
Prepare: begin with comfortable joint movements or a low-intensity rehearsal of the planned evidence while breathing normally.
Practice: apply the movement cues for coaching a tactical idea to someone else at a self-selected challenge, resting or reducing the range whenever control changes.

Apply: perform, simulate, diagram, gesture, or fully describe coaching a tactical idea to someone else under the authored transfer condition and preserve every required cue, decision, comparison, or revision. Full transfer credit requires the designed constraint, the tactical decision it is meant to produce, the coaching cue, and a success check. Live coaching or a full solo simulation earns equal credit when it preserves all four pieces of evidence.
Finish: transition to easy movement or rest, then name one safety check and one adjustment for next time. No score, measurement, photo, or recording is needed beyond the stated transfer evidence.
privacySafeScenario: Design a constraints-led practice that forces a specific tactical decision, run it, and evaluate whether the decision improved — then teach the idea to one other person or write the coaching script.
studentTask: Learner works coaching a tactical idea to someone else through a constraint-led practice the learner designs and either coaches to an available participant or fully simulates with a diagram and written coaching script at a self-set intensity, then records what held, what degraded first, and how this occasion differed from the earlier one. Full transfer credit requires the designed constraint, the tactical decision it is meant to produce, the coaching cue, and a success check. Live coaching or a full solo simulation earns equal credit when it preserves all four pieces of evidence.
knowledgeCheck: In one concise response, say which feature of coaching a tactical idea to someone else degraded first under the added demand, why, and what you would change before the next attempt.
completionCriteria: The learner clears or accurately describes the safe space and selects the standard, accessible, or no-equipment path for coaching a tactical idea to someone else.

The learner performs or fully models coaching a tactical idea to someone else under the authored transfer condition and supplies the stated cue, decision, comparison, or revision evidence. Full transfer credit requires the designed constraint, the tactical decision it is meant to produce, the coaching cue, and a success check. Live coaching or a full solo simulation earns equal credit when it preserves all four pieces of evidence.
The learner identifies the equipment choice (including none), one safety or stop rule, and one technique adjustment or next step.

A seated, supported, reduced-range, solo, low-space, no-equipment, simulated, diagrammed, or described version earns equal credit only when it preserves the same transfer evidence. Full transfer credit requires the designed constraint, the tactical decision it is meant to produce, the coaching cue, and a success check. Live coaching or a full solo simulation earns equal credit when it preserves all four pieces of evidence.

Work solo or with one trusted adult. The adapted path is assessed for the same control, decision, and explanation and earns equal credit. Full transfer credit requires the designed constraint, the tactical decision it is meant to produce, the coaching cue, and a success check. Live coaching or a full solo simulation earns equal credit when it preserves all four pieces of evidence.
extensionChallenge: Design the next progression of coaching a tactical idea to someone else yourself, or coach the transfer condition to someone else so that they succeed with it — without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.
Practice may be run live, walked through, simulated on paper, or modelled on a diagram; the tactical reasoning is what is assessed.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to notice where coaching a tactical idea to someone else shows up outside the session under real conditions. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or public performance is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
This task never requires maximal effort, exercise as punishment, or movement through pain.
This task never requires gym access, specialized equipment, or a purchase; the no-equipment path earns equal credit.
